title: Scalable logical qubits
authors: Matthias Troyer, Chetan Nayak, John Martinis
abstract: Utility-scale quantum computing will require executing long, complex algorithms with end-to-end error rates far below what physical qubits can support directly. Error-corrected logical qubits are needed to achieve this goal. To make the progress on logical qubits measurable and comparable we introduce the definition of scalable logical qubits: logical qubits preserved for long computations by repeated quantum error correction, capable of fault-tolerant universal operations with low-latency real-time decoding and feedback, and replicable to the hundreds or thousands, as required by applications. We characterize these scalable logical qubits along four coupled dimensions: reliability, scale, capability, and performance, and discuss trade-offs among these dimensions.
summary: This paper establishes a rigorous framework for measuring progress toward utility-scale quantum computation by defining 'scalable logical qubits.' It characterizes progress across four coupled dimensions—reliability, scale, capability, and performance—and emphasizes that system cost, balancing error correction overhead against runtime, is the ultimate metric. This provides a necessary roadmap for researchers building fault-tolerant quantum processors.
main_problem: Achieving utility-scale quantum computing requires error rates far below what physical qubits can support directly, necessitating robust error correction.
main_result: The authors introduce the concept of 'scalable logical qubits,' characterizing progress across four coupled dimensions: reliability, scale, capability, and performance.
method: The paper defines a rigorous metric for progress by analyzing the trade-offs inherent in quantum error correction (QEC) schemes.
model_or_system: The focus is on abstract quantum error correction codes (e.g., surface codes, LDPC codes) used to encode logical qubits redundantly across physical qubits.
key_observables: Logical error rates ($\epsilon$), number of logical qubits ($N$), logical cycle time, and physical-to-logical qubit overhead.
important_parameters: Target error rates ($\sim 10^{-12}$ to $10^{-15}$), required physical qubit count scaling ($O(N \log \epsilon^{-1})$), and decoding latency.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of low-latency, real-time decoding and feedback mechanisms necessary for fault-tolerant operation.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the necessity of logical qubits, defines the four characterization dimensions (Reliability, Scale, Capability, Performance), discusses the trade-offs between these dimensions, and concludes by framing progress assessment around overall system cost.
why_interesting: It provides a comprehensive, multi-dimensional framework for assessing the maturity of quantum hardware, which is crucial for theorists designing algorithms or analyzing resource requirements for future quantum simulations.
